justifications.layering: Data flows from source to staging to intermediate to marts using refs throughout, with raw sources read only in staging (mon_source_duplicates excepted), and int_f1__session_results feeds both fct_results and fct_session_results so they cannot drift; however int_f1__driver_profiles refs marts (fct_results, fct_session_results, mart_driver_season_standings) and the monitoring model mon_late_arriving_drivers, int_f1__qualifying_entries refs fct_qualifying/fct_results (an inverted dependency), and the 60000 ms red-flag cutoff is hard-coded in mart_race_pit_lane_times, mart_pit_lane_time_trend and mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.
justifications.naming: Prefixes stg_f1__/int_f1__/fct_/dim_/mart_/mon_, _ms suffixes and per-folder _<area>__models.yml files are consistent and easy to navigate, but the Vendor B raw tables are declared under the f1_raw source in staging/f1/_f1__sources.yml even though their models live in staging/vendor_b, while telemetry gets its own _telemetry__sources.yml.
justifications.testing: Source contract tests (columns present, unexpected columns, value format) in _f1__sources.yml plus tests/generic/source_contract.sql would catch the ticket-5 vendor migration, and duplicates_are_identical, assert_fact_row_counts_preserved, assert_constructor_points_reconcile and assert_driver_points_reconcile_with_standings would catch the ticket-6 Ferrari fan-out; keys are tested at staging and business rules at marts (assert_standings_match_official_champions), and models/_unit_tests.yml has about 35 targeted unit tests.
justifications.quirks: macros/parsing.sql handles \N and empty strings (clean_text), uses regex-guarded casts to stop 'E' parsing as 0, and parses multi-format times (time_to_ms); standings are taken from the official snapshot because of sprint points and pre-1991 dropped scores, shared drives are handled by the result_id grain and per-classification podium counting, int_f1__race_calendar defines completed seasons, red-flag stops over 60 s are excluded, and placeholder rows cover late-arriving drivers; each is listed in the README's 'Known data quirks' section.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: fct_lap_times, fct_stints and fct_telemetry use delete+insert on race_id (idempotent whole-race replacement) with a correction window (lap_times_correction_window_races) or a watermark lookback (telemetry_lookback_minutes), fct_stints rebuilds a race off laps_loaded_at, and snp_drivers sensibly uses the check strategy with hard_deletes: invalidate; minor nits are that the lap correction window counts races rather than time (older corrections only raise the warn-level assert_lap_times_match_source), stg_f1__lap_times dedupes on lap_time_ms, which is an arbitrary tie-break, and on_schema_change is 'fail' on the lap/stint models but 'append_new_columns' on fct_telemetry.
justifications.change_hygiene: Later tickets refactored rather than bolted on (dim_drivers was moved into int_f1__driver_profiles with thin v1/v2 selects, and mart_teammate_head_to_head was rewritten on the shared int_f1__qualifying_entries); there is no commented-out code or TODOs, but some docs drifted: the README layout table and _docs.md still say every mart is 'access: public, contracts enforced' after ticket 7 made only fct_results and dim_drivers public.
justifications.docs: Nearly every model and column has a description, reusable doc blocks live in models/_docs.md, and the SQL headers and README explain why things are done a certain way (standings not summed from results, the green-lap definition, the Ferrari incident root cause, measured telemetry partition-rewrite costs, how the Vendor B matcher works).
justifications.interfaces: fct_results and dim_drivers are public in the f1_analytics group with enforced contracts and primary_key constraints, dim_drivers has v1/v2 with deprecation_date 2027-01-01, an alias that keeps DIM_DRIVERS stable for SQL readers, a disabled latest_version_pointer guarded by assert_dim_drivers_v1_window_open, a migration guide in the README, and version-specific unit tests (dim_drivers_v1_keeps_full_name_for_placeholders and dim_drivers_v2_splits_names_for_placeholders).
justifications.open_ended: docs/leadership_questions.md, mart_driver_vs_teammates and mart_pit_lane_time_trend use teammate-relative qualifying gaps adjusted for teammate strength, Wilson intervals, trust tiers and a two-signal verdict, plus circuit-adjusted pit-lane time within the post-2013 speed-limit regime; the doc states confounders (selection bias, number-one status, the 2020 calendar) and pushes back that the 'car' is unobservable and that the data measures pit-lane time, not stationary crew time.

biggest_strength: Defensive engineering against vendor change: source contract and format tests, staging dedupe with conflicting-duplicate errors, fan-out row-count guards and points reconciliation against official standings (tests/singular/*), plus a clone_baseline/compare_to_baseline runbook in macros/ops/baseline.sql, so the ticket-5 and ticket-6 failure classes are caught at the source before numbers change downstream.
biggest_weakness: Layering inversions: intermediate models (int_f1__driver_profiles, int_f1__qualifying_entries) depend on marts and on a monitoring view, and business constants such as the 60 s red-flag cutoff are copied across three marts instead of defined once, which weakens the otherwise clean DAG.
